clue.text: Schoolboy bard is free to charter

indicators.note: free says the letters of 'bard is' are set loose and put back in a new order

parts.note: to charter a boat or plane is to hire it

explanation.surface: A school pupil who writes poems is at liberty to draw up a charter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Schoolboy bard' reads as one person, but 'Schoolboy' alone is the definition. Darbishire is Jennings's best friend in Anthony Buckeridge's stories about a boys' boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Darbishire is a fictional prep-school pupil, so he is an example of a schoolboy.

clue.text: A song taken up by a Duke's wife in Ephesus

parts.note: D is the usual abbreviation for duke

indicators.note: taken up in a down clue says the words for a song are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: an air is a song

explanation.surface: A duke's wife in Ephesus picks up a song.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'taken up' reverses ANAIR to RIANA, which goes below A and D. Adriana is the wife of Antipholus of Ephesus in The Comedy of Errors.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Comedy of Errors, Adriana is married to Antipholus of Ephesus.

clue.text: The fifth child's retrousse nose

indicators.note: retrousse, the word for an upturned nose, says the word is turned up, so read upwards

parts.note: neb is a dialect word for a beak or nose

explanation.surface: The fifth child in a family has a turned-up nose.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben is the strange fifth child in Doris Lessing's novel The Fifth Child.
explanation.definitionFit: Doris Lessing's novel The Fifth Child is about Ben, the troubling fifth baby of the Lovatt family.

clue.text: Nick Ferrars's secret fiancée we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the surname is said out loud to give a word spelt differently

parts.note: in Austen's Sense and Sensibility, Edward Ferrars is secretly engaged to Lucy Steele

explanation.surface: Nick Ferrars is talked about as having a secret fiancée.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a first name for Ferrars, but it is the definition. Lucy Steele is the woman Edward Ferrars is secretly engaged to.
explanation.definitionFit: To nick is British slang for to steal, and both mean to take something without permission.

clue.text: Crane, maybe one a bishop put outside church, lifting door periodically

indicators.note: put outside says the first group of letters wraps round the abbreviation for church

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: lifting in a down clue says the chosen letters are read upwards, so backwards
periodically says every other letter of 'door' is used

explanation.surface: A crane, perhaps, is placed by a bishop outside church to lift a door now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crane' looks like a bird or a machine but is Ichabod Crane of Washington Irving's Legend of Sleepy Hollow. In a down clue 'lifting' reads the picked letters upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ichabod Crane is the schoolmaster in The Legend of Sleepy Hollow, so 'Crane, maybe' points to his first name.

clue.text: Consumers of former poet, start to finish

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: start to finish says the first letter of the poet's name is moved to the end

parts.note: Stephen Spender was an English poet

explanation.surface: Somebody hints at the users of a one-time poet's work, from beginning to end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to finish' moves the S of SPENDER to the end, giving PENDERS.
explanation.definitionFit: People who spend or use up money or goods are consumers.

clue.text: Family of a house at Allington glen

definitions.text: Family of a house at Allington

explanation.surface: Somebody points out which family lives in a valley house at Allington.
explanation.walkthrough: Trollope's novel The Small House at Allington centres on the Dale family, Lily and Bell Dale among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Trollope's Small House at Allington belongs to the Dales, and a dale is a valley, which is what a glen is.

clue.text: Rude verb misused about sick young villain

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go round the word for sick
misused says the letters of 'Rude verb' are put to wrong use, so rearranged

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: A rude verb is misapplied to a sick young scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'young villain' is Alec d'Urberville, who seduces Tess in Hardy's Tess of the d'Urbervilles; the apostrophe is dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Alec d'Urberville, the wealthy young man who seduces Tess in Hardy's novel, is its villain.

clue.text: Determined Christmas will turn up in part of a Winter's Tale

indicators.note: will turn up in a down clue says both words are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: set means determined, as in set on winning
Noel is another word for Christmas

explanation.surface: Determined that Christmas will show up somewhere in The Winter's Tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will turn up' reverses SETNOEL as a whole, giving LEON then TES.
explanation.definitionFit: Leontes, the jealous King of Sicilia, is a role in Shakespeare's The Winter's Tale.

clue.text: Poet taking year out at sea, missing as a writer

indicators.note: taking ... out, around 'year', says that the word for year is removed from the poet
out completes taking ... out, the instruction to remove the year from the poet's name

parts.note: Lord Byron, the Romantic poet

indicators.note: missing says the letters of 'as a' go absent from the words 'at sea' before them

explanation.surface: A poet who spends a year sailing goes missing as a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... out' takes Y from BYRON, leaving BRON; 'missing' takes A, S and A out of ATSEA, leaving TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte, Emily and Anne Bronte were all novelists, so the surname names a writer.

clue.text: One comes in very excited, performing a titanic poem

indicators.note: comes in says the word for one enters the pair of words built from the rest

parts.note: hyper is slang for overexcited
on stage and performing is being on
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An excitable person bursts in to recite a huge poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Keats's unfinished Hyperion is about the fall of the Titans, so 'titanic' is literal, not just big.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats's Hyperion tells of the Titan Hyperion and his overthrow, so it is a poem about Titans.

clue.text: King in an ancient trap penned by crooked novelist

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for king goes inside the words for an ancient

parts.note: an ancient thing is an old one
R, from Latin rex, abbreviates king

indicators.note: penned by says the trap is shut up inside the word for crooked, as if in a pen

parts.note: a crooked dealer is bent
a net is a trap for fish or birds

explanation.surface: A king caught in an old snare that a dishonest author has written about.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one picture of a king in a trap, but the clue splits in two after 'ancient', each half a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnold Bennett wrote The Old Wives' Tale and the Clayhanger novels, so he was a novelist.

clue.text: Quiet evening wind supports 'light-winged Dryad'

indicators.note: supports in a down clue says the word for wind sits below and holds up what is above it

parts.note: a night in is a quiet evening spent at home
a gale is a strong wind

explanation.surface: A gentle evening breeze holds up a wood nymph.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition quotes Keats's Ode to a Nightingale, which calls the bird 'light-winged Dryad of the trees'.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats addresses the songbird in his Ode to a Nightingale as 'light-winged Dryad of the trees'.

clue.text: A scary film editor visiting Dynmouth's Timothy by car

parts.note: Jag is short for a Jaguar car

indicators.note: visiting says the editor drops in, going inside the surname

parts.note: Timothy Gedge is the boy in William Trevor's novel The Children of Dynmouth

explanation.surface: A horror-film editor calls on a character from a William Trevor novel, travelling by car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just puts the car beside the rest. Jagged Edge is a 1985 courtroom thriller with a masked killer.
explanation.definitionFit: Jagged Edge is a 1985 thriller about a masked killer, a film meant to frighten.

clue.text: Sign to see above centrepiece in credit to Markham

indicators.note: centrepiece in says the letters are found in the middle of 'credit to Markham'

explanation.surface: A sign telling readers to see above sits in the middle of an acknowledgment to Markham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centrepiece in' points to the run between the C-R-E of credit and the H-A-M of Markham.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of commas-like marks under a word tells the reader to repeat the item written above.

clue.text: Very flip intro is cut from a Patrick White novel

indicators.note: intro is cut says the opening letter of the word for flip is removed

parts.note: to flip a coin is to toss it

explanation.surface: Somebody makes a glib remark cut from the start of a Patrick White book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intro is cut' takes the first letter T off TOSS, leaving OSS.
explanation.definitionFit: Voss (1957), about a German explorer crossing Australia, is one of Patrick White's best-known novels.

clue.text: Who did dial M?' said Bond

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads "Who did dial M?' said Bond" with no opening quotation mark, so it looks cut short at the start; KNOT is a bond and sounds like 'not', but the words that should say 'not' are missing.
annotationWithheld.clue: Who did dial M?' said Bond

clue.text: Cloud nymph's short relative fled unclothed

indicators.note: short says the word for the relative loses its last letter

parts.note: a nephew is a relative

indicators.note: unclothed says 'fled' loses its outer letters, as if stripped

explanation.surface: A cloud nymph's undersized relative ran off naked.
explanation.walkthrough: Nephele is the cloud nymph of Greek myth, mother of Phrixus and Helle. 'short' cuts NEPHEW to NEPHE; 'unclothed' strips 'fled' to LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nephele is a nymph in Greek myth whom Zeus made out of a cloud, and her name is Greek for cloud.

clue.text: Fool with university room beginning to enjoy a Peake novel

parts.note: tit is British slang for a fool
a salon is a reception room

indicators.note: beginning to says only the first letter of 'enjoy' is used

explanation.surface: A fool with a college room starts to enjoy a Mervyn Peake novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Titus Alone is the third Gormenghast book by Mervyn Peake.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus Alone (1959) is the third of Mervyn Peake's Gormenghast novels.

clue.text: Operas mostly include energy as part of them

indicators.note: include says the abbreviation for energy is taken inside the shortened operas
mostly says the operas' title loses its last letter

parts.note: The Ring is Wagner's four-opera cycle
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Operas mostly feature energy among their elements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operas' stands for Wagner's Ring cycle, The Ring, a stretch of crossword licence the solver has to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Therein means in that place or thing, so it fits inside the people or things just mentioned.

clue.text: Books covering Eastern God of war most closely

indicators.note: covering says the books wrap round the eastern god

parts.note: NT, the New Testament, is a set of books
Ares is the Greek god of war

explanation.surface: Books covering the eastern god of war are studied in detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Books' is a common crossword stand-in for the New Testament or Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearest means closest, which is what most closely means.

clue.text: Mahler epic on a new recording device

indicators.note: new says the letters of 'Mahler epic on a' are made over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A Mahler epic gets a new recording on some device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recording' suggests sound after 'Mahler', but this device records images: a camera with a tiny hole in place of a lens.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera captures and records an image, and this kind uses a tiny hole in place of a lens.

clue.text: A college missing its top poetry book

indicators.note: missing its top in a down clue says the college name loses its first letter

parts.note: Oriel is an Oxford college

explanation.surface: A college lacks the first volume of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing its top' cuts ORIEL to RIEL. Ariel is Sylvia Plath's famous last collection of poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel (1965) is the collection of poems by Sylvia Plath published after her death.

clue.text: Poet being married in a state after wife goes missing (4)

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for married goes inside the state's name
goes missing says the abbreviation for wife is removed from the state's name

parts.note: Delaware is a US state

explanation.surface: A poet marries in some state after his wife disappears.
explanation.walkthrough: The '(4)' after 'missing' is printed in the clue as held; the enumeration is (2,2,4) for Walter de la Mare.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter de la Mare wrote The Listeners and other well-known poems.

clue.text: A faithful princess maiden filling Zeus's lover with information

indicators.note: filling says the maiden sits inside the name of the god's lover

parts.note: Io was loved by Zeus and turned into a heifer
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A loyal princess and a young girl fill in Zeus's lover with the facts.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Cymbeline, Imogen stays true to her husband Posthumus even after he is tricked into thinking she has been unfaithful.
explanation.definitionFit: Imogen, the King's daughter in Cymbeline, stays loyal to her banished husband through every trial.

clue.text: In bed she protested about love

parts.note: on means about, as in a book on birds
love is zero in tennis, and O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A woman lies in bed protesting about love.
explanation.walkthrough: Yoko Ono and John Lennon staged their 1969 bed-ins for peace.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoko Ono and John Lennon staged bed-ins in 1969, staying in bed as a peace protest.

clue.text: This man is the Gods' cupbearer

parts.note: he is the pronoun for this man
is is a form of the verb to be

explanation.surface: Someone announces that this man pours the wine for the gods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This man' makes the solver think of Ganymede, the male cupbearer, but here it only gives HE. The cupbearer is the goddess Hebe, who held the job before Ganymede.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the goddess Hebe served nectar to the Olympians before Ganymede took the post.

clue.text: Nothing in the work spoilt one by Scott

indicators.note: in says the word for nothing goes inside the jumbled letters
spoilt says the letters of 'the work' are messed up into another order

parts.note: nil means nothing, a zero score

explanation.surface: Nothing in the piece was ruined by a work of Scott's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one by Scott' means one novel by Sir Walter Scott; Kenilworth is set at the Elizabethan castle of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenilworth (1821) is one of Sir Walter Scott's historical novels.
